title: Oscar Pettiford's playing, and taking Simmons's bass
summary: Praise for Pettiford's solos with Duke and Hawkins; he twice took Simmons's bass overnight.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: Now I remember a record that he made with Duke that just gassed me, 'Airconditioned Jungle'. Jimmy Hamilton had the clarinet solo and Oscar played rhythm and melody right along with him, it was like a duet almost. He carried the melodic line and was playing the rhythm at the same time. And then this solo that he made on the cello Perdido'. Now that sounded like Charlie Christian on guitar almost.

And this solo that he made with Hawk and Eddie Heyward, 'The Man I Love', you could hear him breathing. Boy he could play. But now he's been not knowing anything about positions or tuning up or anything. He'd just pick up a bass, run his hand over it, find out where the notes was and he would hit it every time.

And the bass neck would just be gooyey from perspiration. I come to work one night, my bass wasn't there. I say 'what is this. Somebody stole my bass.' So I proceeded to get drunk. About 12:00 here comes Oscar walking in with my bass. Man, I had a record date to do and I'm sorry to have this overtime, but I couldn't get into the club to get my bass. I was so glad to get my bass, I wasn't mad or angry at him. I say

okay. And this happened again to me at Cafe Society downtown. I don't know who took the bass but they kept it all night, you know and the next night it was back on the bandstand. And I never carried any insurance on my instruments, you know.
